rawFindings.title: Unrestricted `updateAccessControlManager` lets anyone hijack signature verification
rawFindings.description: The `updateAccessControlManager` function can be called by any external address and updates the `accessControlManager` reference used by `DistributionCreator`. The contract does not restrict the caller, nor does it validate the new address.
rawFindings.attackPath: 1. Attacker calls `updateAccessControlManager(maliciousContract)` before the legitimate owner does.
rawFindings.impact: Unauthorized campaign creation, possible loss of user funds, and complete takeover of the reward‑distribution flow.
rawFindings.recommendation: Add `onlyOwner` (or a governor‑only) access control to `updateAccessControlManager` and validate that the new address implements `IAccessControlManager` and is non‑zero.

rawFindings.title: Missing re‑entrancy guard on `toggleDispute` enables double‑spend of dispute funds
rawFindings.description: `toggleDispute` transfers dispute tokens from the caller (if needed) and then calls `distributor.disputeTree(reason)` without any re‑entrancy protection. If `disputeTree` performs an external call (e.g., token transfer or callback) that can re‑enter `toggleDispute`, the attacker can trigger the token‑transfer logic again before the first call finishes.
rawFindings.impact: Excessive loss of dispute‑token escrow, potentially emptying the dispute fund and allowing the attacker to force disputes without covering the required amount.
rawFindings.recommendation: Add a `nonReentrant` modifier (e.g., OpenZeppelin’s `ReentrancyGuard`) to `toggleDispute` or restructure the function to perform external calls after all state changes.
